title: Low-touch POC hosting guidance for small-batch pilots
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a lightweight, repeatable approach for onboarding small-batch customer POCs (1–5k monthly active users, limited dataset footprint) where the customer wants a quick demonstration of product fit without heavy ops overhead. Target audience: solutions engineering, sales engineers, and customer platform teams who need a low-friction hosting recommendation and a checklist for risk mitigation.

Context and motivation:
- We frequently see customers who want to validate an LLM integration quickly but cannot commit to Dedicated capacity or a full Private deployment during discovery.
- The goal is to provide a neutral, low-risk hosting pattern that:
  - Minimizes cost and setup time for both Redwood and the customer,
  - Preserves an upgrade path to Dedicated or Private as the pilot scales,
  - Addresses common early concerns (data residency, throughput, latency, and auditability) with minimal engineering lift.

Customer profile suitable for this pattern:
- Startup or midmarket product team with prototype SLAs (soft latency targets e.g., <400ms p50),
- Low to moderate sensitivity data (PII allowed with contract controls; PHI/PCI will require additional controls),
- Expecting to validate product/UX before committing to capacity reservations,
- Technical contact available for short-lived connector or proxy setup (1–2 engineers).

Decision criteria (quick checklist to select this path):
- Time-to-first-demo: need a working POC in <= 2 weeks? -> favors Low-touch hosted baseline.
- Scale expectations: peak QPS < 50 and concurrent requests < 10 in early weeks -> OK.
- Data sensitivity: no regulated data, or customer comfortable with a short-term data processing agreement -> OK.
- Cost cadence: prefers usage billing over monthly commits -> OK.

Recommended hosting pattern (one-page summary):
1) Baseline: Hosted (Redwood API) as the canonical default for low-touch POCs
   - Why: fastest onboarding (API key, simple SDK), no infra setup, fullest set of platform features (observability, streaming, function-calling).
   - Short-term mitigations: limit model size to optimize cost (e.g., 13B family instead of 70B), enable prefix caching where appropriate, apply per-route quotas.

2) Optional enhancement: Hosted + Private Connector (tunnel) for sensitive payloads
   - Use case: customer requires traffic routing through their VPC for auditability but doesn't want full Private.
   - Pattern: small reverse-tunnel or proxy that sends only metadata/IDs to Redwood while embedding encrypted blobs for transient processing (TTL keys).
   - Trade: slightly more setup (VPN/SSH tunnel or managed connector) but avoids full on-prem installation.

3) If latency is critical and hosted baseline fails SLOs: Dedicated mini-pool as an intermediate step
   - Reserve minimal Dedicated GPUs (e.g., 1 GPU pool or shared reserved capacity with burst) to keep latency predictable while maintaining Redwood-managed ops.

Detailed tradeoffs (hosted vs dedicated vs private) for this customer archetype:
- Hosted (fastest):
  - Pros: time-to-demo, lowest ops burden, full platform telemetry, cost = pay-as-you-go.
  - Cons: perceived control concerns, multi-tenant inference runtime (logical isolation), egress/residency constraints for some customers.
- Dedicated (middle):
  - Pros: predictable latency/throughput, SLA option, stronger isolation.
  - Cons: time and procurement for capacity reservation, higher baseline cost.
- Private (heavy):
  - Pros: full network isolation, customer owns control plane, required for strict compliance.
  - Cons: longest lead time, most ops overhead, potential compatibility integration work.

Quick cost/latency heuristics (ballpark for RD estimate):
- Hosted with 13B model: token cost low, expected p50 latency 150–350ms for short prompts; egress/storage negligible for small pilots.
- Dedicated single-GPU pool (V100/A10 equivalent) for low concurrency: baseline latency 80–200ms, monthly committed cost high relative to pilot usage.
- Private on-prem tiny cluster: large setup cost, amortized only for enterprise.

POC runbook (step-by-step, low-touch):
1) Initial kickoff (Day 0–1): collect success metrics, data examples, acceptance criteria, security constraints.
2) Demo scaffolding (Day 1–3): set up hosted API key, create simple proxy route in Redwood Console, push a minimal prompt set and small eval suite.
3) Observability hooks (Day 3–5): enable route-level tracing, token cost tracking, and error alerts; wire up Slack channel for alerts.
4) Customer verification (Day 5–7): run synthetic load tests, gather latency/cost snapshots, iterate on prompt / model sizing.
5) Final review and decision (Week 2): present results, recommend next steps (continue hosted, switch to Dedicated, or start Private planning).

Acceptance criteria (example measurable checkpoints):
- Functional: 95% of target user flows produce acceptable outputs per the prompt evaluation set.
- Latency: p50 < 400ms and p95 < 800ms on customer sample traffic (hosted baseline).
- Cost: projected per-1k-requests cost within the customer's approved budget band.
- Security: data handling aligned with the signed Data Processing Addendum for the pilot.

Common pitfalls and mitigations:
- Surprise cost growth: set strict per-route quotas and alerts, sample token-level dashboards before live demo.
- Data leakage worries: redact PII in example dataset or use synthetic substitutes; propose temporary DPA language early.
- Latency bursts under load: enable autoscaling/burst or cap concurrency; run small synthetic spike tests to reveal issues.

Templates and tickets to create at kickoff:
- SE-Pilot-Checklist (Confluence page) — create and share with customer.
- Jira: SE-842 (POC setup), SE-843 (observability hook), INF-211 (optional Dedicated sizing).
- GH: fork of demo app with environment README and example prompts (link above).

Open questions / decision points for this customer:
- Does legal accept a short-term DPA permitting hosted processing? If not, plan moves to Private connector or Private deployment.
- Are there concrete latency SLAs that would force Dedicated on day 1? If yes, request QPS/latency targets from customer.
- Which model families are acceptable for the customer (cost vs quality tradeoff)?

Next steps (owners and timeline):
- [Maya Chen] Draft the SE-Pilot-Checklist and runbook (2 business days).
- [Samir Khan] Validate connector feasibility with infra team if customer requests tunnel (3 business days).
- [Laura Gómez] Prepare cost snapshot and two model-size alternatives for conversation (1 business day).
- [Devon Price] Create demo app PR with environment variables and example prompts (2 business days).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the pilot narrow — feature gating helps containment.
- Save a canonical prompt/eval set for reuse across similar customers (reduces lead time).
- For customers teetering on security needs, present Hosted + Connector as a pragmatic compromise.

Attachments / references (internal):
- Quick latency testing script (gh://redwood-inference/tools/poc-loadtest).
- Example DPA clause snippet (confluence://spaces/Legal/pages/pilot-dpa-snippets).

End of doc.
